title: Electric fields of charge distributions by integration; Electric flux and Gauss's law; Maxwell's equations overview
qualification: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: F06-calc-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; F06-calc-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; F07-calc-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; F06-calc-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: F06-calc-1#N.4, F06-calc-2#N.2, F07-calc-1#N.4, NEW-maxwell-equations-1#N.2, F06-calc-1#N.6, F06-calc-2#N.5, F07-calc-1#N.7, NEW-maxwell-equations-1#N.7, F06-calc-1#N.9, F06-calc-2#N.7, F07-calc-1#N.9, NEW-maxwell-equations-1#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electric flux
items.clue: Measure of how much field passes through a surface, in N m²/C.

items.label: Gaussian surface
items.clue: Any closed, imaginary 3D shape; it can pass through empty space.

items.label: Charge element
items.clue: Tiny piece dq of a rod or ring, treated as a small source of dE.

items.label: Area vector
items.clue: Has a size equal to the extent of a surface and points at right angles to it.

questions.stem: An open hemispherical surface of radius R, shaped like a bowl with no flat base, is in a uniform electric field of magnitude E. The field is parallel to the hemisphere's axis of symmetry. What is the magnitude of the electric flux through the hemispherical surface?
For which of the following can Gauss's law, with a suitably chosen Gaussian surface, be used to calculate the magnitude of the electric field at the stated point?

options.text: A very long, uniformly charged solid cylinder, at a point 3 cm from its axis
A uniformly charged solid cube, at a point 1 cm from the center of one of the cube's faces
A uniformly charged rod 20 cm long, at a point 3 cm from the midpoint of the rod
A sphere with +Q on its upper half and −Q on its lower half, at a point far from it

questions.stem: A thin rod of length L, with charge +Q spread uniformly along it, lies on the x-axis from x = 0 to x = L. The magnitude of the electric field at point P, at x = −L, is E₁. The rod is replaced by a rod of length 2L, with the same charge +Q spread uniformly, lying from x = 0 to x = 2L. The magnitude of the field at P is now E₂. What is the ratio E₂/E₁?
Gauss's law is the first of Maxwell's equations, the set of equations that together fully describe electromagnetism. Which statement about Gauss's law is correct?

options.text: It holds for highly symmetric charge distributions and fails for others.
It gives the field of any charged object when the Gaussian surface matches its shape.
It is Coulomb's law restated, so it holds for point charges but no others.
It holds for every closed surface, whatever charges lie inside or outside it.

questions.stem: A closed surface encloses two small beads with charges +2.0 nC and −6.0 nC. A third bead, with charge −3.0 nC, is outside the surface. What is the net electric flux through the closed surface? Use ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/(N·m²).

Two large, parallel metal plates, each of area A, are far from other objects, and their separation is much smaller than their dimensions. One plate carries a net charge +4Q and the other carries a net charge −Q. Which expression gives the magnitude of the electric field between the plates, away from their edges?

A thin, insulating rod is bent into a semicircle of radius 0.15 m and carries charge +4.0 nC spread uniformly along its length. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the center of the semicircle? Use k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C².

An electron is held at rest at a point outside a long solenoid, where the solenoid's magnetic field is negligible. The current in the solenoid begins to increase, and the electron is released. Which describes the force on the electron just after it is released?

options.text: An electric force directed along a radius, toward the solenoid's axis
An electric force tangent to a circle around the solenoid's axis
A magnetic force, as the flux through its circle around the axis changes
No force, as the magnetic field is negligible where the electron is

questions.stem: A point charge +q is at the center of a thin, insulating spherical shell of radius R. The shell carries charge −3q spread uniformly over its surface. What are the magnitude and direction of the electric field at a distance r > R from the center?

A thin, flat, insulating disk of radius R carries a surface charge density that varies with distance r from its center as σ(r) = σ₀(1 − r²/R²), where σ₀ is a positive constant. What is the total charge on the disk?

A thin rod of length L carries charge Q spread uniformly. Point P is on the rod's perpendicular bisector, a distance y = L/2 from the rod. What is the magnitude of the electric field at P, as a multiple of kQ/L²?
questions.explanation: E = kQ/(y√(y² + L²/4)) with y = L/2: kQ/((L/2)√(L²/2)) = 2√2 kQ/L² ≈ 2.8 kQ/L².

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is being charged, with a steady current in the wires connected to its plates. Which statement about the region between the plates is correct?

options.text: There is no magnetic field, because no charges move across the gap between the two plates.
The increasing electric field between the plates produces a magnetic field that circles that region.
A magnetic field is present, produced by the electric field and lasting while that field remains.
A magnetic field is present, produced by charges carried across the gap from plate to plate.
